fatal_errors: The W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr refractory alloy is intrinsically heavy and therefore conflicts with the lightweight-alloy requirement.
The proposed composition and laser-cladding route do not reconstruct the MgAlTiVFeCo ball-milling and SPS route.
Al2O3 formation is proposed even though the specified alloy contains no aluminum.
The 2.83 J/mm threshold is transferred from selective laser melting of NbMoTaW to laser cladding of a different alloy without supporting validation.
The Cr-Hf order-disorder boundary is irrelevant because the proposed alloy contains no Hf.
The falsification experiment omits aqueous corrosion testing despite corrosion resistance being a central claimed outcome.
explanation: The response addresses a multi-principal alloy, hardness, oxidation, corrosion, BCC stability, and provides a testable oxidation experiment, but it diverges from the target in composition, processing, temperature window, structural mediator, and quantitative outcome. It misses SPS densification and the 800–1000 °C Mg-volatilization boundary, as well as the oxide barrier phases AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3. Its chromia-based mechanism has only generic overlap with diffusion-controlled protective-scale formation. Evidence E1 supports studying laser-clad WVTaTiCr coatings, but the proposed Cr range, annealing regime, submicron grains, hardness, oxidation improvement, and phase-suppression claims are largely extrapolated from different materials and processes. The experiment can test parts of the alternative oxidation mechanism, but it cannot discriminate the claimed aqueous-corrosion mechanism and lacks comparison in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
